selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What important item is described as being in his hand?
questions.answer: A message from the Lord of the universe, which is the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the passage show that many people accepted this message over time?
questions.answer: It says that in every century, more than three hundred million people accepted and confirmed it.

questions.question: How many kinds of wonder are mentioned for this decree?
questions.answer: Seven.

questions.question: What other number is given to show the Qur’an’s extraordinary nature?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an has forty aspects of miraculousness.

questions.question: According to the passage, whose word is the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It is the word of the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why does the passage not explain all the proofs in detail here?
questions.answer: Because it says those proofs were already explained fully in another well-known work.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveller make about the one who delivers and announces this decree?
questions.answer: He says such a person cannot be lying.

questions.question: What is the main subject of this passage: worship, law, or the truthfulness of the messenger?
questions.answer: The truthfulness of the messenger.

questions.question: What title is used for the message he carries?
questions.answer: It is called the Qur’an of Mighty Stature.

questions.question: What does the passage say people did with this decree in each century?
questions.answer: They received it with acceptance and affirmation.

questions.question: What does the passage use to support the claim that the Qur’an is amazing?
questions.answer: It mentions several kinds of wonder and says strong proofs were given elsewhere.

questions.question: What moral problem would happen if the messenger lied while delivering the decree?
questions.answer: He would be unfaithful both to the message and to the One who sent it.

questions.question: What can we infer about the rank of the decree from the way it is described?
questions.answer: It has very high status and is far above ordinary human speech.

questions.question: What overall argument does the passage build from the Qur’an to the messenger?
questions.answer: It argues that the greatness and divine source of the Qur’an support the honesty of the one who brings it.

questions.question: From whom does the decree come?
questions.answer: It comes from the Lord of the universe.

questions.question: What does the repeated acceptance of the decree across centuries suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests lasting influence and wide trust among people.

questions.question: What two numerical details are used to emphasize the Qur’an’s greatness?
questions.answer: The passage mentions seven ways of wonder and forty aspects of miraculousness.

questions.question: What claim is made about the source of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The claim is that it comes from the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why is another book mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It is mentioned as the place where the detailed evidence has already been presented.

questions.question: What does the traveller say about the person who conveys this decree?
questions.answer: He says there is no way such a person could be a liar.

questions.question: What reason is given for that impossibility?
questions.answer: Lying would oppose the message itself and would be disloyal to the One who revealed it.

questions.question: What does the passage say the messenger is doing with the decree?
questions.answer: He is carrying it and announcing it to people.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur’an’s special nature in a short way?
questions.answer: It describes it as extraordinarily wondrous and miraculous.

questions.question: What does the phrase about every century help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see that belief in the Qur’an continued strongly through time.
